hero.headline: US economy adds 57,000 jobs in June, missing forecasts by half
hero.body:
The US labor market showed unexpected weakness in June, with employers adding just 57,000 jobs according to data released Thursday by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The figure fell dramatically short of economist expectations, which had projected roughly 110,000 new jobs for the month. The unemployment rate declined slightly to 4.2 percent, down from 5.3 percent in May.

The disappointing jobs report has significant implications for Federal Reserve policy decisions. Labor market data serves as a key indicator for policymakers evaluating interest rate adjustments and broader monetary policy. A substantial miss on job creation can signal economic softening or shifts in employer hiring behavior. Analysts suggest the weak figures could reduce pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise rates in coming months.

Some had anticipated the World Cup hosted by the US would boost hiring, particularly in hospitality and related sectors. However, leisure and hospitality employment actually declined by 61,000 in June, reflecting weaker than usual seasonal hiring patterns. This underperformance disappointed those expecting a jobs boost from increased tourism and event-related activity.

Job gains were concentrated in limited sectors. Professional and business services added 36,000 positions, while social assistance gained 25,000 jobs, primarily in individual and family services. Health care employment rose by 22,000. Employment showed little to no change across mining, construction, manufacturing, wholesale trade, retail trade, transportation, information technology, financial activities, and government sectors.

The jobs report also revealed downward revisions to previous months. April's job growth was revised down by 31,000, from 179,000 to 148,000, while May's figure was reduced by 43,000, from 172,000 to 129,000. This pattern raises questions about whether earlier strength in job reports reflected temporary demand rather than sustainable employment trends.

Despite weak job creation, the slight decline in the unemployment rate to 4.2 percent presents a mixed picture. The number of unemployed people fell to 7.094 million from 7.307 million in May. However, labor economists typically analyze job creation and unemployment figures together to assess overall labor market health. A declining unemployment rate coupled with weak job growth may indicate workers leaving the labor force rather than securing employment.

Financial markets responded to the report. The US dollar declined on foreign exchange markets following the weak employment data, pushing the pound to a two-week high. Traders interpreted the hiring slowdown as potentially reducing the likelihood of near-term interest rate increases from the Federal Reserve.

The June employment figures mark a significant shift from the previous three months, all of which had surprised to the upside before revisions. Analysts and investors are now reassessing whether the fundamental strength supporting economic growth in the second quarter will persist in coming months.

cards.headline: Russian Strikes Kill at Least 18 in Kyiv After Ukraine Hits Deep Into Russia
cards.body:
Russian forces launched a massive overnight attack on Kyiv using drones and missiles, killing at least 18 people and injuring 86 others, according to local authorities. The death toll may still rise as emergency crews continue searching through rubble.

The assault struck residential buildings across several districts of Ukraine's capital, with fires breaking out at multiple locations. A hotel on one of Kyiv's central boulevards was also hit. The intensity of the bombardment forced many residents to shelter in subway stations as loud explosions shook the city for hours.

Kyiv's mayor declared a day of mourning following what officials described as one of the most massive Russian assaults on the capital in recent months. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky had warned days earlier that Moscow was preparing a large-scale strike in response to Ukrainian operations hitting deeper into Russian territory.

The attack reflects an intensifying pattern in the conflict. Ukraine has carried out some of its longest-distance drone strikes deep inside Russia, targeting the country's oil sector and other strategic infrastructure. These operations have damaged Russian refineries and military fuel supplies. In response, Russia has maintained its strategy of launching devastating attacks on Ukrainian population centers rather than altering its military approach.

According to Zelensky, Russia used drones, cruise missiles, and a significant amount of ballistic weapons in the latest assault. "Most of the targets are ordinary infrastructure in cities," he stated on social media. "Residential buildings, energy, and enterprises have been damaged."

The overnight bombardment also extended beyond Kyiv. Ukrainian authorities reported that Odesa and Kharkiv were targeted by drones, with at least three people injured in those cities. Authorities said they repelled most of more than 600 Russian drones launched during what appears to have been the largest attack in several days.

In Russia, a woman was killed and a man seriously injured when Ukraine struck the border region of Belgorod with drone strikes.

The escalation comes as Russia and Ukraine conducted a prisoner exchange on Friday, in which both sides exchanged 193 service members. These periodic exchanges were among the conditions outlined in US-brokered negotiations between Moscow and Kyiv, though those talks have delivered no progress on key issues needed to end Russia's invasion.

The exchange of increasingly intense strikes represents a new phase in the conflict, with Ukraine demonstrating expanded offensive capabilities while Russia continues to target major Ukrainian cities and civilian infrastructure. The broader regional security concerns generated by the intensified fighting prompted Poland to scramble jets and Finland to restrict its airspace.

cards.headline: Google loses appeal of $4.7 billion EU antitrust fine over Android practices
cards.body:
The European Union's top court upheld a $4.7 billion antitrust fine against Google on Thursday, rejecting the tech giant's appeal of a 2018 penalty related to its Android operating system. The Court of Justice of the European Union ruled that Google used Android to illegally block rivals from competing in the mobile market.

The fine, equivalent to 4.1 billion euros, represents one of the largest antitrust penalties ever imposed by European regulators. The European Commission originally issued the penalty after determining that Google required smartphone manufacturers to pre-install Google Search and the Chrome browser as a condition for licensing the Google Play app store. Regulators found these practices prevented competing search engines and browsers from gaining market share on Android devices.

Google had challenged the Commission's findings, arguing that Android created more choice for consumers and that device makers remained free to install competing apps. The company maintained that its arrangements were necessary to support the free distribution of Android and fund continued development of the operating system. The appeal process stretched across multiple years as Google sought to overturn or reduce the penalty.

The ruling marks a significant victory for European antitrust enforcement and sets a precedent for how regulators can address market dominance in digital platforms. Android powers roughly 70 percent of smartphones globally, giving Google substantial control over how hundreds of millions of people access internet services. The decision affirms the Commission's authority to challenge business practices that leverage dominance in one market to gain advantages in adjacent markets.

The fine adds to a series of European penalties against major American technology companies. Google faces separate EU investigations and fines related to its advertising technology and shopping comparison services. The company must now pay the full penalty, which European authorities can collect directly from Google's operations if the company does not comply voluntarily. Google has not indicated whether it will change its Android licensing practices in response to the ruling.

cards.headline: Germany's Leaders Strike Economic Deal to Counter Far Right Gains
cards.teaser: Chancellor Friedrich Merz and center-left coalition partners agreed on economic reforms aimed at jump-starting growth and holding off hard-line political rivals.
cards.body:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz reached an agreement with his center-left coalition partners on economic measures designed to revitalize the country's sluggish economy. The deal comes as far-right parties have gained ground in polls and recent regional elections.

The agreement includes politically difficult compromises that leaders hope will demonstrate the governing coalition's ability to address voter concerns about economic stagnation. German officials view the economic package as critical to preventing further erosion of support to hard-line rivals who have capitalized on public frustration with slow growth and rising costs.

cards.headline: US confirms it will not extend North American trade deal for 16 years
cards.teaser: The United States declined to grant a lengthy extension to the regional trade agreement but did not pursue more aggressive changes.
cards.body:
The United States has confirmed it will not extend the North American trade agreement for another 16-year term. The decision represents a more restrained approach than some had anticipated, as officials avoided the escalated confrontation that observers had expected surrounding the pact's future.

By stopping short of more dramatic action, US officials maintained room for future negotiations on trade terms while keeping tensions in check with North American partners.

cards.headline: Trump administration offers limited Iranian oil sanctions relief
cards.teaser: The Trump administration has moved toward easing some oil sanctions on Iran as part of broader negotiations.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has taken steps toward providing limited relief on Iranian oil sanctions, a move that has drawn criticism from some foreign policy observers and lawmakers. The administration has framed the decision as part of ongoing diplomatic negotiations with Tehran.

Critics have argued that any sanctions relief provides economic benefits to Iran's government without sufficient guarantees in return. Supporters of the approach maintain that diplomacy requires making difficult choices between imperfect agreements and no diplomatic progress at all, particularly when dealing with complex international relationships involving nuclear programs and regional security concerns.

cards.headline: Trump earned over $1 billion from crypto ventures in 2025, filing shows
cards.teaser: President Trump and his family took in more than $1 billion last year through cryptocurrency businesses, according to a federal financial disclosure.
cards.body:
President Trump and his family earned more than $1 billion through cryptocurrency businesses in 2025, according to a federal financial disclosure filed Wednesday. The crypto income significantly exceeded his earnings from real estate and Trump-branded products like watches.

The disclosure requirement, mandated by federal ethics rules, applies to presidents and other high-ranking officials. The filing provides insight into the Trump family's financial activities as cryptocurrency has become an increasingly important sector of the U.S. economy.

cards.headline: Vatican Excommunicates Society of St. Pius X in First Major Crisis for Pope Leo
cards.teaser: The Vatican excommunicated the traditionalist Society of St. Pius X after the group defied Pope Leo XIV by consecrating new bishops without papal approval.
cards.body:
The Vatican declared the Society of St. Pius X in schism and excommunicated its bishops and priests after the traditionalist group consecrated new bishops without papal consent. The move came after repeated warnings from Pope Leo XIV went unheeded.

The Society of St. Pius X has long operated in tension with Rome over its rejection of reforms from the Second Vatican Council. The excommunications represent a significant challenge for the pontiff's early papacy.

cards.teaser: Chancellor Friedrich Merz and center-left coalition partners agreed on economic reforms aimed at jump-starting growth and holding off hard-line political rivals.

cards.headline: Truck Driven by Boy Kills Nine Buddhist Monks in Thailand
cards.teaser: A pickup truck crashed into a group of monks walking on pilgrimage in northeast Thailand, killing nine and injuring eleven others.
cards.body:
Nine Buddhist monks were killed when a pickup truck driven by an 11-year-old boy collided with a religious procession in northeast Thailand. Eleven others were injured in the crash.

The monks, part of a group of 35 religious members and five lay followers, were walking by the roadside when the truck struck them. Thai authorities are investigating the circumstances of the accident and how the boy came to be driving the vehicle.

cards.headline: China Identifies Pilot Who Crashed Plane Into Beijing Skyscraper
cards.teaser: Beijing authorities said the pilot who crashed a plane into a city skyscraper had suffered from insomnia and anxiety and had expressed suicidal thoughts.
cards.body:
Chinese authorities have identified the pilot involved in a plane crash into a Beijing skyscraper. Officials stated that the pilot had experienced insomnia and anxiety, and had expressed suicidal intentions prior to the incident.

The collision damaged the tower, leaving visible holes in its structure. The revelation about the pilot's mental health struggles has raised concerns about aviation security protocols and how airlines monitor the psychological well-being of flight crew members.

cards.headline: Putin Maintains Assault Strategy Despite Ukrainian Strikes on Russian Territory
cards.teaser: Russian President Vladimir Putin has responded to Ukrainian attacks inside Russia by continuing strikes on Ukrainian cities rather than changing his military approach.
cards.body:
President Vladimir Putin has responded to Ukraine's expanded military operations inside Russia by intensifying attacks on Ukrainian cities. A major Russian assault on Kyiv using ballistic missiles and drones killed at least 17 people, prompting the city's mayor to declare a day of mourning. A nine-storey residential building was completely destroyed in the attack.

Ukraine has struck Russian oil facilities and other infrastructure supporting military operations. Rather than shifting tactics to counter these Ukrainian advances, Putin has maintained his pattern of targeting civilian population centers through continued drone and missile strikes on the capital.

cards.headline: Polish Jets Scrambled and Finland Restricts Airspace During Russian Strike on Ukraine
cards.teaser: Poland deployed fighter jets and Finland imposed airspace restrictions as Russia launched a major assault on Kyiv, highlighting regional security concerns.
cards.body:
Poland scrambled military aircraft and Finland restricted its airspace during Russia's large-scale attack on Ukraine's capital. The defensive measures by NATO members reflect the broader security implications of the intensified fighting between Russia and Ukraine.

The coordinated responses from neighboring countries came as Russian forces used ballistic missiles and drones in what Ukrainian officials described as one of the most massive strikes on Kyiv. The actions demonstrate how the expanded conflict affects airspace security and military readiness across the region beyond Ukraine's borders.

hero.headline: House Democrats allege donors misled by Trump-backed Freedom 250 celebration
hero.body:
House Democrats released a report accusing former President Donald Trump of orchestrating a takeover of the United States' 250th anniversary celebration to benefit political allies and advance a Christian nationalist agenda. The congressional investigation found evidence of corruption, wire fraud, and pay-to-play schemes tied to the event.

According to a House Democratic subcommittee report titled "From Vanity to Insanity: How the White House Cheated the American People Out of Their 250th Birthday," Trump and his associates allegedly used the Freedom 250 celebration to enrich themselves while misleading donors about how their contributions would be used. The investigation uncovered what Democrats describe as a shadow corporation embedded within the National Park Foundation that facilitated the alleged misconduct.

The report outlines multiple concerning practices. Donors who believed they were supporting a major national commemoration of America's founding anniversary say they received insufficient information about where their money would actually go. The Democrats allege the event prioritized spectacle and political gain over genuine historical significance and public education.

Federal funds flowed to firms connected to Trump advisers during the planning and execution phases of the celebration. Reports indicate the Freedom 250 failed to deliver on its promotional promises, disappointing contributors who expected a major national event. Instead, critics characterized it as an empty state fair that did not meet advertised standards or educational goals.

The investigation represents the latest congressional scrutiny of financial arrangements involving Trump associates. House Democrats argue that the disconnect between marketing materials and the actual event warrants transparency about how federal and private donor funds were allocated.

The subcommittee's findings suggest that Trump used the 250th anniversary commemoration to serve multiple purposes beyond celebrating American independence. Democrats claim the event functioned as a vehicle for promoting Christian nationalist ideology and harvesting voter data, in addition to enriching Trump's political allies.

The report calls attention to what lawmakers describe as conflicts of interest when private business ventures become intertwined with public commemorations. House Democrats are pushing for clearer financial disclosures and accountability mechanisms to prevent similar situations in future national celebrations.

The controversy reflects broader concerns about how Trump associates have monetized projects bearing his endorsement. As historians note the unprecedented scale of Trump's financial gains from various ventures, lawmakers emphasize the need for stricter oversight of commemorative events that combine federal resources with private fundraising.

The Freedom 250 case demonstrates the complications that arise when political figures control major national celebrations, according to Democratic critics. They argue that donors and the American public deserve transparency about how commemorative events are financed and executed, particularly when federal funds are involved.

cards.headline: Two arrested after climbing Empire State Building, apparently to get engaged
cards.teaser: A daredevil couple scaled the Empire State Building in New York City and are now in custody awaiting arraignment.
cards.body:
Russian "rooftoppers" Angela Nikolau and Ivan Beerkus scaled the Empire State Building's spire on Wednesday, reaching well above the areas open to the public. The pair spent at least ten minutes at the top of the 1,454-foot landmark before climbing down.

While atop the building, they unfurled a large black banner displaying the message: "When the power of love beats the love of power the world knows peace." The couple apparently got engaged during the climb. Both were arrested and are awaiting arraignment. Nikolau and Beerkus have conducted similar urban climbing stunts in other cities including Tianjin, China, and Los Angeles.

cards.headline: Shark attack on Alabama teen prompts launch of national alert system
cards.teaser: An attack on a teenager in Alabama has inspired officials to begin implementing a nationwide shark alert system.
cards.body:
A shark attack on an Alabama teenager has led to the development and initial rollout of a national alert system designed to warn beachgoers of potential dangers. The incident, which affected a young person on the Alabama coast, served as the catalyst for creating a coordinated warning network.

The new system aims to provide timely information to swimmers and surfers about shark activity along American coastlines. Officials hope the alert network will help prevent future attacks by giving the public advance warning when sharks are spotted in popular beach areas.

cards.headline: Trump denies conflict of interest over cryptocurrency business ventures
cards.teaser: Former President Trump has denied any conflict of interest after reports showed his family earned over $1 billion last year from crypto and other businesses.
cards.body:
Donald Trump and his family earned over $1 billion through cryptocurrency ventures in 2025, according to financial disclosures released by the US Office of Government Ethics. The president's total earnings for the year exceeded $2.2 billion, including income from real estate, golf resorts, branded merchandise, licensing deals, and court settlements.

Lawmakers including Senator Elizabeth Warren have called the earnings "brazen crypto corruption" and demanded tighter regulations on political figures' cryptocurrency dealings. Trump has denied that his family's crypto ventures create conflicts of interest despite the substantial financial stakes involved.

cards.headline: Influencer Nara Smith receives support after revealing daughter's cancer diagnosis
cards.teaser: Social media influencer Nara Smith disclosed that her toddler daughter Whimsy Lou was diagnosed with cancer late last year.
cards.body:
Influencer Nara Smith shared an emotional video announcing that her young daughter Whimsy Lou was diagnosed with cancer in late 2025. The disclosure prompted an outpouring of support from her followers and fellow content creators.

Smith, known for her significant social media presence, opened up about her family's experience following the diagnosis, marking a deeply personal moment for the influencer.

cards.headline: Rescuers work to free earthquake survivor trapped for eight days
cards.teaser: Emergency workers continue efforts to rescue Hernán Gil, who has been trapped since an earthquake more than a week ago.
cards.body: Hernán Gil has survived eight days trapped following an earthquake, with rescue teams working over 100 hours to free him. Emergency workers have provided him with an intravenous drip as they work to extract him from the rubble. Throughout the operation, Gil has been encouraging the rescuers as they make progress toward his extraction.

cards.headline: Russian attack on Kyiv kills at least 18 people
cards.teaser: Ukraine's capital suffered a major drone and missile attack that killed at least 18 people, prompting a day of mourning.
cards.body:
Russia launched a massive combined drone and missile attack on Kyiv overnight, killing at least 18 people and injuring 86 others, according to local authorities. Fires broke out across multiple districts as strikes and debris hit residential buildings and a central hotel. Emergency services warned the death toll could rise as rescue operations continued.

Kyiv's mayor declared a day of mourning following the assault, describing it as the most significant Russian attack on the Ukrainian capital in recent times. The strike tested the city's air defense systems as the assault targeted civilian infrastructure throughout the capital.

cards.headline: Rivian raises 2026 delivery forecast after strong second quarter demand
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker increased its full-year delivery outlook following higher-than-expected customer orders in the second quarter.
cards.body:
Rivian has raised its 2026 delivery forecast following strong second-quarter performance. The electric vehicle maker expects to deliver several thousand additional vehicles by the end of 2026 compared to previous projections, driven by increased production capacity and robust customer demand.

The positive outlook was bolstered by the recent launch of Rivian's next-generation R2 SUV, which contributed to improved sales momentum during the quarter. The company's production ramp-up at its manufacturing facilities supported higher delivery volumes in the period.

cards.headline: Jobs report expected as labor market conditions put pressure on Federal Reserve
cards.teaser: New employment data scheduled for release Thursday comes as recent hiring gains intensify debate over interest rate policy.
cards.body:
The Labor Department will release June employment figures on Thursday as the Federal Reserve weighs monetary policy decisions. Strong hiring gains in recent months have intensified pressure on the central bank to consider raising interest rates to combat potential economic overheating.

The timing of the jobs report coincides with a critical juncture for monetary policy. Federal Reserve officials are balancing inflation concerns against economic growth prospects. Robust employment data could support the case for tighter monetary policy, while disappointing hiring figures might allow the Fed to maintain current interest rate levels.

cards.headline: Beef prices reach record highs as Americans continue buying steak
cards.teaser: Consumers are paying historically high prices for beef products, yet demand remains strong heading into the Fourth of July holiday.
cards.body:
Steak and other beef products are selling at record prices across the United States, with costs rising significantly compared to previous years. Despite the price increases, consumer demand for beef has not declined, particularly as Americans prepare for Fourth of July cookouts and summer grilling.

Multiple factors have contributed to elevated beef prices, including production costs and supply chain dynamics in the cattle industry. The sustained demand despite higher prices reflects consumer willingness to pay premium rates for beef products during peak grilling season.

cards.teaser: The United States declined to grant a lengthy extension to the regional trade agreement but did not pursue more aggressive changes.

cards.headline: UK car finance compensation payments pushed to next year
cards.teaser: Millions of consumers who may be entitled to compensation over car loan commission arrangements will face delays in receiving payments.
cards.body:
Millions of people could be entitled to compensation from car finance commission arrangements between lenders and dealers. The payments have been delayed until next year, pushing back the timeline for affected borrowers to receive funds.

The compensation stems from how dealers received commissions on car loans sold to consumers. Regulators have investigated whether these commission structures created conflicts of interest that led consumers to pay higher interest rates than necessary.

cards.headline: Stock futures trade mixed ahead of June jobs report
cards.teaser: US stock index futures showed little movement Thursday morning as investors awaited employment data with markets closed Friday for the holiday.
cards.body:
Stock futures for major US indexes traded without clear direction Thursday morning following a weak start to July trading. Investors positioned ahead of the June jobs report release, which could influence Federal Reserve policy decisions in coming months.

Markets will be closed Friday for the Independence Day holiday, compressing trading activity into Thursday's session. Oil prices pulled back further as traders assessed supply and demand dynamics in energy markets.

hero.headline: Scientists build first synthetic cell with complete life cycle
hero.body:
Researchers have created what they describe as the first fully synthetic cell capable of completing an entire life cycle, including growth and division. The achievement, which scientists have named SpudCell, represents a significant advance in synthetic biology and biological engineering.

The synthetic cells were constructed from chemical compounds rather than material extracted from existing living organisms. Built from the ground up in laboratory conditions, they are believed to be the first to demonstrate the complete cell cycle of growth, genetic replication and splitting to produce the next generation.

Dr Kate Adamala, who led the research at the University of Minnesota, explained the significance of the work. "It is not as robust, as fast, or as good at most of its functions as a natural cell, but it is proof of principle that molecules can reconstitute behaviours that up until now we only associated with natural living cells," she said. "If we want to be able to engineer biology, we really have to understand exactly the blueprint, every component of it, so we know what we're changing."

Adamala's team built SpudCells starting with tiny water-filled spheres called liposomes, which measure a few thousandths of a millimetre wide. They added synthetic DNA to provide basic cellular functions. The name evokes both Sputnik and the space age, though Adamala, who is Polish, also chose it as a personal reference to potatoes.

SpudCells function only within a liquid rich in vital chemicals such as ATP, the main energy-carrying molecule that living cells normally manufacture from nutrients. To grow, SpudCells fuse with smaller "feeder" liposomes that contain molecules, enzymes and ribosomes needed for protein production. The synthetic genome carries instructions for copying itself and dividing.

However, SpudCells have significant limitations. They cannot build their own protein-making machinery, control their metabolism or clear their waste. They rely completely on the substances and components in the surrounding liquid. Additionally, they often pass on incorrect amounts of DNA when dividing and typically cease functioning after a few generations.

Prof Tom Ellis from Imperial College London called the work probably the field's "biggest breakthrough in recent times." The achievement provides a fully understood system for testing biological circuits and computer models of cellular life while helping scientists understand the minimum requirements for life.

The development raises the prospect of artificial organisms designed and built to produce drugs, foods, fuels and other materials. Adamala and others are launching an institution called Biotic to advance SpudCells into something more capable. The goal, according to co-founder Prof Drew Endy from Stanford University, is to build "an operating system for life" made from genes and biochemistry.

The study was released as a preprint before peer review, allowing other laboratories to examine the work without delay.

cards.headline: Amazon activates satellite internet service to compete with Starlink
cards.teaser: Amazon has launched enough satellites to begin operating its broadband internet service, entering direct competition with SpaceX's Starlink network.
cards.body:
Amazon has activated its satellite internet service after deploying 396 satellites to low-Earth orbit. The company, which operates the service under the Amazon Leo brand, now has sufficient coverage to provide continuous service across its initial service areas. The milestone was reached following the final Atlas V rocket launch, which carried 29 broadband satellites to orbit from Florida.

The deployment establishes Amazon as a competitor in the satellite internet market alongside SpaceX's Starlink. Amazon Leo aims to deliver broadband connectivity to regions where traditional ground-based infrastructure is limited or unavailable.

cards.headline: NASA delays rescue mission for Swift space telescope due to rocket problem
cards.teaser: A rocket issue has postponed NASA's launch of a mission intended to boost the Swift Observatory back into a stable orbit.
cards.body:
NASA has delayed the launch of a mission designed to rescue the Swift space telescope after identifying an issue with the rocket scheduled to carry the rescue spacecraft. The Swift Observatory, which has been operating in orbit, requires a boost to maintain its position and continue operations.

The mission was intended to deploy a spacecraft that would dock with Swift and push it back into a higher orbit. The telescope has been gradually losing altitude, and without intervention, it would eventually fall from orbit. NASA has not provided a new launch date for the rescue mission.

cards.headline: China's Tianwen-2 spacecraft reaches quasi-moon Kamooalewa
cards.teaser: A Chinese space probe has arrived at Kamooalewa, a small object that follows an orbit near Earth and may be a fragment of the Moon.
cards.body:
China's Tianwen-2 spacecraft has likely reached Kamooalewa, a quasi-moon that shadows Earth's orbit. The small celestial body may be a piece of the Moon that was blasted into space by an ancient impact. The mission aims to collect a sample and return it to Earth.

Kamooalewa follows an orbit that keeps it relatively close to Earth, though it is not a true moon. Scientists believe studying samples from the object could provide information about the Moon's composition and the history of impacts in the Earth-Moon system. The Tianwen-2 probe is China's fifth venture in its planetary exploration program.

cards.headline: Google electricity use jumped 37% in 2025 due to AI data centers
cards.teaser: Google's power consumption increased sharply as the company expanded data centers to support artificial intelligence operations.
cards.body:
Google's electricity consumption surged 37 percent in 2025 as the company expanded data centers to power its artificial intelligence systems. The massive computing infrastructure needed to train and operate AI models has become a major driver of the company's energy demands.

Google is working to offset the environmental impact through clean energy investments. The company's challenge is managing the substantial power requirements of its AI operations while reducing associated emissions.

cards.headline: Sony decision to eliminate physical game discs draws strong opposition
cards.teaser: A survey shows 86 percent of respondents oppose Sony's plan to stop producing physical discs for PlayStation games.
cards.body:
A poll by Digital Foundry with approximately 45,000 votes found that 86 percent of respondents believe Sony should reconsider its decision to eliminate physical game discs. Sony has announced it will end physical disc production for all new PlayStation games by 2028, transitioning to digital-only distribution.

Critics have expressed concerns about game preservation and long-term access to digital titles. Meanwhile, Microsoft is reportedly developing a disc-to-digital feature that would allow Xbox owners to convert their existing physical game collections to digital versions, potentially offering an alternative approach as the industry shifts toward all-digital distribution.

cards.headline: Xbox testing system to convert physical games to digital copies
cards.teaser: Microsoft is reportedly developing a feature that would allow Xbox users to digitize their physical game collections.
cards.body:
Microsoft is developing a disc-to-digital feature that would let Xbox owners convert their physical game collections into digital versions accessible in their libraries. The system is designed to work with games from the Xbox One era onward.

The feature represents Microsoft's response to changing industry trends as it prepares its next-generation console, codenamed Project Helix. This move aligns with Sony's recent decision to phase out physical game disc production for future PlayStation consoles.

hero.headline: Celtics trade Jaylen Brown to 76ers in NBA free agency stunner
hero.body:
The Boston Celtics have traded 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers in a major offseason transaction that reshapes the Eastern Conference. Boston will acquire Paul George, two first-round picks from 2028 and 2031, and two second-round selections in the deal.

The trade concludes a tumultuous period for Brown with the Celtics. The All-Star had expressed unhappiness with his treatment by the franchise in recent weeks, leading to the blockbuster move that fundamentally alters both teams' rosters heading into the upcoming season.

For the 76ers, the acquisition adds a proven two-way wing and a player who just captured Finals MVP honors. Brown's combination of scoring ability and defensive prowess gives Philadelphia a significant boost as the team aims to contend for a championship in the Eastern Conference.

The Celtics return to rebuilding mode with this transaction, acquiring established star power in Paul George while also gathering additional draft capital for future roster construction. The deal signals Boston's willingness to pivot its roster strategy following the previous season's championship run.

This trade represents one of the most significant moves in the current free agency period, which has already seen multiple franchises making aggressive roster changes. Teams across the league have been active in pursuing overhauls during the opening days of the signing period, with various combinations of trades and signings reshaping competitive landscapes.

The rapid pace of offseason activity has created clear distinctions among franchises. Some teams have positioned themselves advantageously through strategic acquisitions and signings, while others have made moves that analysts question. The Brown-George swap stands out as the centerpiece transaction of free agency so far, illustrating how teams are recalibrating their approaches to championship contention.

The deal also comes amid broader movement throughout the league, with franchises assessing their rosters and making adjustments. Multiple teams are evaluating which moves have improved their championship prospects and which decisions they may come to regret.

The transaction demonstrates how quickly the landscape can shift during free agency, with marquee players finding new homes and teams reconfiguring their core players. Both Boston and Philadelphia are now in the position of integrating new talent while adjusting their overall roster construction around their new acquisitions.

As the offseason continues to unfold, the implications of this trade will likely trigger additional moves as other teams respond to the competitive changes it creates. The Eastern Conference balance of power has been fundamentally altered, setting the stage for continued activity as franchises finalize their rosters for the coming season.

cards.headline: Lakers complete rapid roster overhaul with Kessler trade and free agency signings
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles Lakers executed a swift offseason transformation built around Luka Doncic after the LeBron James era.
cards.body:
The Lakers completed what was described as a 35-minute offseason overhaul, acquiring Walker Kessler in a trade and making multiple free agency moves. The team is constructing its roster with Luka Doncic as the top priority, marking a new direction for the franchise in the post-LeBron era.

Analysts are debating whether the moves make Los Angeles a legitimate contender. The rapid succession of transactions represents a clear strategic shift as the Lakers attempt to position themselves for championship competition with a new core in place.

cards.headline: US forward Folarin Balogun sent off in World Cup match against Bosnia-Herzegovina
cards.teaser: The American striker received a red card in the second half of the World Cup group stage match.
cards.body:
Folarin Balogun scored the opening goal in the United States' 2-0 victory over Bosnia-Herzegovina, marking his third goal of the tournament. The Monaco striker was among the US's standout performers on the pitch.

However, roughly 20 minutes after his goal, Balogun was shown a straight red card for contact with Bosnia defender Tarik Muharemović. The dismissal appeared to stem from inadvertent contact during which Balogun's foot made contact with his opponent's ankle. The ejection left the USMNT playing with 10 men for the remainder of the match, despite their eventual advancement to the World Cup last 16.

cards.headline: England's World Cup win over DR Congo draws 16.3 million BBC viewers
cards.teaser: The dramatic last-16 victory attracted a massive television audience in the United Kingdom.
cards.body:
England's dramatic World Cup last 16 victory over DR Congo attracted 16.3 million viewers on the BBC, making it one of the tournament's most-watched matches.

The strong audience numbers reflect the intensity of the knockout fixture as England advanced through the competition's final stages.

cards.headline: USMNT defeats Bosnia-Herzegovina despite playing without top scorer
cards.teaser: The United States demonstrated versatility in advancing at the World Cup with Belgium up next.
cards.body:
The United States men's national team defeated Bosnia-Herzegovina 2-0 in the World Cup round of 32, securing its first knockout victory since 2002. The win came despite a significant setback when star striker Folarin Balogun was sent off in the second half following a collision with Bosnia's Tarik Muharemović.

Playing down a man, the USMNT responded with resilience. Malik Tillman scored to put the Americans through to the last 16, demonstrating the team's ability to overcome adversity in crucial matches.

cards.headline: Finn Russell ruled out as Scotland names squad for Argentina match
cards.teaser: Jonny Gray returns to the squad after missing the Six Nations tournament earlier this year.
cards.body:
Scotland will be without fly-half Finn Russell for their opening Nations Championship match against Argentina this summer. The absence of the experienced playmaker represents a significant blow as the team begins its summer international campaign.

Jonny Gray has been recalled to the squad following his absence from this year's Six Nations. The return of the experienced forward bolsters Scotland's options as they prepare for the Argentina fixture.

cards.headline: Jockey Frankie Dettori hospitalized with broken ribs after car crash
cards.teaser: The racing jockey is recovering in the hospital following the accident.
cards.body:
Frankie Dettori, the 55-year-old jockey, is recovering in hospital after a car accident in Newmarket on Wednesday evening. Another vehicle struck the rear passenger side of his car, causing it to flip. He sustained broken ribs and a broken thumb in the incident.

Dettori remains hospitalized while his injuries continue to be assessed. His management company H Talent Management confirmed the details of the accident.

hero.headline: Influencer Nara Smith Reveals Toddler Daughter Diagnosed With Cancer
hero.body:
Social media influencer Nara Smith shared that her toddler daughter Whimsy Lou was diagnosed with cancer late last year. Smith disclosed the news in an emotional video posted to her social media accounts.

The announcement prompted an outpouring of support from followers and other content creators. Smith, known for her lifestyle content, had not previously made the diagnosis public. The specific type of cancer and treatment details were not included in the video.

Smith's disclosure comes months after the initial diagnosis, suggesting the family has been managing the situation privately while treatment has been underway. The influencer has built a significant following through her social media presence, making the personal revelation reach a wide audience.

The response from the online community has been substantial, with messages of encouragement flooding Smith's social media channels. Childhood cancer diagnoses affect thousands of families annually, with treatment protocols varying based on cancer type and stage at detection.

Smith's decision to share her daughter's health struggle publicly reflects a growing trend among social media personalities who balance their public personas with private family challenges. The influencer has not indicated whether she plans to document the treatment journey or maintain greater privacy moving forward.

cards.headline: Graham Norton and Phoebe Waller-Bridge Spotted in New York Ahead of Rumored Taylor Swift Wedding
cards.teaser: Celebrities including Graham Norton and Phoebe Waller-Bridge have been seen arriving in New York before what is rumored to be Taylor Swift's wedding.
cards.body:
Multiple high-profile figures have been spotted arriving in New York ahead of what sources describe as Taylor Swift's wedding. Among those seen were television host Graham Norton and actress Phoebe Waller-Bridge.

The sightings have fueled speculation about an upcoming ceremony, though no official confirmation has been released. Swift has not publicly commented on wedding plans or the gathering in New York.

cards.headline: President Trump Posts AI Video Targeting Celebrity Critics Including Rosie O'Donnell and Robert De Niro
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump shared an AI-generated video on Truth Social depicting himself as a doctor treating celebrity critics for what he calls Trump Derangement Syndrome.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump posted an AI-generated video to his Truth Social account late Wednesday night. The video depicts Trump as a doctor and targets several celebrity critics, including Rosie O'Donnell, Whoopi Goldberg, and Robert De Niro.

The post uses the term "Trump Derangement Syndrome," which Trump has previously employed to characterize opposition to his administration. The video was shared just before the July 4 holiday weekend.

cards.headline: Canal+ Stops Distributing TF1 Group Channels After Negotiations Break Down
cards.teaser: Pay-TV company Canal+ Group has ceased distribution of several TF1 Group channels in France, Switzerland, and Africa following failed negotiations.
cards.body:
Canal+ Group stopped distributing multiple channels from French broadcaster TF1 Group across France, Switzerland, and Africa after negotiations between the companies collapsed. The distribution halt affects viewers across three continents.

The move follows TF1 Group's recent launch of a distribution partnership with Netflix in France. Since June 19, Netflix subscribers in France have been able to access TF1 content through the streaming platform, marking a significant shift in the French broadcasting landscape.

cards.headline: British Independent Production Company Proper Content to Close After Nearly 10 Years
cards.teaser: Award-winning factual producer Proper Content is shuttering due to market conditions, with founder David DeHaney citing lack of commissioning opportunities.
cards.body:
Proper Content, an independent factual production company, will cease operations and appoint an administrator, founder David DeHaney announced. DeHaney established the company in 2016, and it operated for nearly a decade producing factual programming.

DeHaney described the decision as very difficult and cited challenging market conditions. He specifically pointed to a lack of commissioning opportunities, stating there simply is not the commissioning risk in the current environment.

cards.headline: Latin Recording Academy CEO Says English No Longer Required for International Success
cards.teaser: Manuel Abud told a Taiwan music conference that Latin artists no longer need to record in English to achieve global reach, pointing to changes in the industry.
cards.body:
Manuel Abud, CEO of the Latin Recording Academy, told attendees at Taiwan's 2026 Golden Melody Festival that the traditional path to international success for Latin artists has shifted. For decades, recording in English was considered necessary for global reach, but Abud explained that approach no longer applies.

The session took place at the Golden Melody Festival conference, held ahead of Taiwan's Golden Melody Awards. The annual event brings together music industry leaders from across regions to discuss trends and changes in the global music landscape.

cards.headline: Music Supervisor Brittany Whyte Discusses Storytelling Role at Taiwan Festival
cards.teaser: Brittany Whyte, whose credits include The Hunger Games and The Handmaid's Tale, spoke about music supervision extending beyond song selection.
cards.body:
Brittany Whyte, music supervisor for The Handmaid's Tale, Riverdale, and The Hunger Games: Catching Fire, presented at the 2026 Golden Melody Festival in Taiwan. Her session explored how music supervision extends beyond song selection to serve broader storytelling purposes in film and television.

Whyte emphasized that music supervision is a multifaceted craft involving far more than choosing great songs. The presentation highlighted how supervisors strategically deploy music to enhance narrative and character development across productions.

hero.headline: US economy adds 57,000 jobs in June, missing forecasts by half
hero.body:
The US labor market showed unexpected weakness in June, with employers adding just 57,000 jobs according to data released Thursday by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The figure fell dramatically short of economist expectations, which had projected roughly 110,000 new jobs for the month. The unemployment rate declined slightly to 4.2 percent, down from 5.3 percent in May.

The disappointing jobs report has significant implications for Federal Reserve policy decisions. Labor market data serves as a key indicator for policymakers evaluating interest rate adjustments and broader monetary policy. A substantial miss on job creation can signal economic softening or shifts in employer hiring behavior. Analysts suggest the weak figures could reduce pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise rates in coming months.

Some had anticipated the World Cup hosted by the US would boost hiring, particularly in hospitality and related sectors. However, leisure and hospitality employment actually declined by 61,000 in June, reflecting weaker than usual seasonal hiring patterns. This underperformance disappointed those expecting a jobs boost from increased tourism and event-related activity.

Job gains were concentrated in limited sectors. Professional and business services added 36,000 positions, while social assistance gained 25,000 jobs, primarily in individual and family services. Health care employment rose by 22,000. Employment showed little to no change across mining, construction, manufacturing, wholesale trade, retail trade, transportation, information technology, financial activities, and government sectors.

The jobs report also revealed downward revisions to previous months. April's job growth was revised down by 31,000, from 179,000 to 148,000, while May's figure was reduced by 43,000, from 172,000 to 129,000. This pattern raises questions about whether earlier strength in job reports reflected temporary demand rather than sustainable employment trends.

Despite weak job creation, the slight decline in the unemployment rate to 4.2 percent presents a mixed picture. The number of unemployed people fell to 7.094 million from 7.307 million in May. However, labor economists typically analyze job creation and unemployment figures together to assess overall labor market health. A declining unemployment rate coupled with weak job growth may indicate workers leaving the labor force rather than securing employment.

Financial markets responded to the report. The US dollar declined on foreign exchange markets following the weak employment data, pushing the pound to a two-week high. Traders interpreted the hiring slowdown as potentially reducing the likelihood of near-term interest rate increases from the Federal Reserve.

The June employment figures mark a significant shift from the previous three months, all of which had surprised to the upside before revisions. Analysts and investors are now reassessing whether the fundamental strength supporting economic growth in the second quarter will persist in coming months.

cards.headline: Trump earned over $1 billion from crypto ventures in 2025, filing shows
cards.teaser: President Trump and his family took in more than $1 billion last year through cryptocurrency businesses, according to a federal financial disclosure.
cards.body:
President Trump and his family earned more than $1 billion through cryptocurrency businesses in 2025, according to a federal financial disclosure filed Wednesday. The crypto income significantly exceeded his earnings from real estate and Trump-branded products like watches.

The disclosure requirement, mandated by federal ethics rules, applies to presidents and other high-ranking officials. The filing provides insight into the Trump family's financial activities as cryptocurrency has become an increasingly important sector of the U.S. economy.

cards.headline: Barrett faces conservative backlash after birthright citizenship vote
cards.teaser: Justice Amy Coney Barrett is drawing fierce criticism from conservative lawmakers and pundits after voting to uphold birthright citizenship.
cards.body:
Justice Amy Coney Barrett joined Chief Justice John Roberts, Justice Brett Kavanaugh and the Supreme Court's three liberal justices in upholding birthright citizenship. The decision struck down President Trump's executive order targeting the practice, dealing a significant blow to a core element of his immigration agenda implemented on his first day in office.

The ruling has sparked intense backlash from conservative lawmakers and commentators who expected Barrett to side with the administration on immigration enforcement. Conservative critics have leveled both political attacks and sexist remarks against the justice following her vote to preserve citizenship rights established under the 14th Amendment.

cards.headline: Colorado governor fires clemency board members over Tina Peters dispute
cards.teaser: Governor Jared Polis removed two clemency board members after they publicly opposed his commutation of former clerk Tina Peters' prison sentence.
cards.body:
Colorado Governor Jared Polis removed two clemency board members on Wednesday after they publicly opposed his decision to commute Tina Peters' prison sentence. Azra Taslimi and Hannah Seigel Proff confirmed their dismissals to CNN.

Peters, a former state elections clerk, was convicted for her involvement in efforts to interfere with election processes related to the 2020 presidential election. Polis's choice to reduce her sentence proved controversial among board members who either were not consulted or disagreed with the commutation.

cards.headline: Republicans confront stalled legislative agenda ahead of midterms
cards.teaser: Speaker Mike Johnson and Senate Majority Leader John Thune face the reality that completing their pre-midterm priorities appears increasingly unlikely.
cards.body:
Speaker Mike Johnson and Senate Majority Leader John Thune are confronting the likelihood that key items on their legislative agenda will not be completed before the midterm elections. The acknowledgment represents a significant setback for Republican leadership, which had set ambitious goals for the legislative session.

The stalled agenda comes as Congress faces a compressed calendar and ongoing divisions within the Republican caucus over policy priorities and strategy. With midterm elections approaching, the window for passing major legislation continues to narrow, potentially forcing leadership to scale back expectations or push key votes into the post-election period.

cards.headline: Hegseth to host National Guard ceremony for America 250 celebrations
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth will host a ceremony Thursday morning with National Guard troops as part of America 250 events.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth will host a ceremony Thursday morning with National Guard troops to commemorate America's 250th anniversary. The event will showcase the Trump administration's DC Safe and Beautiful Task Force, an initiative aimed at improving security and beautification efforts across the nation's capital.

The ceremony is part of broader celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of American independence, with the DC Safe and Beautiful Task Force serving as a key priority for President Trump's administration to enhance federal facilities and public spaces in Washington.

cards.headline: Trump administration offers limited Iranian oil sanctions relief
cards.teaser: The Trump administration has moved toward easing some oil sanctions on Iran as part of broader negotiations.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has taken steps toward providing limited relief on Iranian oil sanctions, a move that has drawn criticism from some foreign policy observers and lawmakers. The administration has framed the decision as part of ongoing diplomatic negotiations with Tehran.

Critics have argued that any sanctions relief provides economic benefits to Iran's government without sufficient guarantees in return. Supporters of the approach maintain that diplomacy requires making difficult choices between imperfect agreements and no diplomatic progress at all, particularly when dealing with complex international relationships involving nuclear programs and regional security concerns.
